::: {.callout-note .se-question appearance="simple"}
## The question

[Why did he take out the $i$ from this equation?](https://math.stackexchange.com/questions/2519883/why-did-he-take-out-the-i-from-this-equation), asked by [fpsshubham](https://math.stackexchange.com/users/480896/fpsshubham) on Mathematics Stack Exchange (2017-11-14; [CC BY-SA 3.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/3.0/)):

> If he wants the imaginary part then why did he remove the $i$ symbol from the last part?
>
> [![derivation][q-1]][q-1]
>
>
>
>   [q-1]: 2u3gJ.jpg
:::

The imaginary part is the coefficient of $i$ in a complex number.  So by itself it's a real number.

If $z=x+iy$ is a complex number, then the imaginary part of $z$ is $y$, not $yi$.
